title: [finding] service-analytics still spells a year below 1000 its own way: `formatDateBucket` labels bucket key `0050` as 1970 and `0050-06` as `50-06`, and the draft-preview `bucketDate` writes unpadded keys the published path no longer writes
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with named producers**. Finding class **(a)**. `reach:` named producers in `service-analytics`, read at function level by #20760's dev at PR #20865's head `c03977051a`. ⛔ A public door was not measured.
- `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dimension-labels.ts` `formatDateBucket`, called by `analytics-service` `resolveDimensionLabels` for a date dimension's key;
- `packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts` `bucketDate`, over a draft dataset's seed rows (`?preview=`).

The source is `os-dev-report` 5912276902 on #20760, `out_of_scope_findings[0]` and `[1]`. Both are one family, so they are filed as one card.

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01DEvba2nBuD4tWzfq8r8NFY`, `os-support-ai`). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

PR #20865 (#20760) makes every core bucket key spell its year with four digits (`0050`, `0050-Q2`, `0050-06`, `0050-06-15`, `0049-W52`). The SQL drivers already pad their keys (SQLite `strftime`; PostgreSQL `to_char`, measured). Two `service-analytics` functions still spell such years their own way:

| producer | input | answer | right answer |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `formatDateBucket` (a dimension label) | year key `0050` | `1970`: the pure-digit key is read as epoch seconds, because the year recogniser admits only 1000..9999 | `0050` |
| `formatDateBucket` | month key `0050-06`, day key `0050-06-15` | `50-06`, `50-06-15` | the key as written |
| `preview-evaluator` `bucketDate` (draft preview) | an instant on `0050-06-15` | `50` / `50-Q2` / `50-06` / `50-06-15` | `0050` / `0050-Q2` / `0050-06` / `0050-06-15`, as the published dataset path answers |

Quarter and week keys pass `formatDateBucket` unchanged, and a 2026 control is correct on both.

So for years 0001..0999:
- a date dimension's label on a chart can read `1970`;
- a draft's preview buckets differ from what the same dataset answers once published.

## Scope for whoever takes it (⛔ not a ruling)

- `formatDateBucket` recognises every key core's `bucketDateKey` writes, the four-digit year from 0001 included, and relabels nothing it did not write.
- `bucketDate` delegates to `bucketDateKey` for its keys, as `bucketKeyAtOrdinal` now does (PR #20865). ⛔ No second padding.
  - Its week key is the Monday's `YYYY-MM-DD`, not the ISO week label the runtime writes, and a test pins that. Whether preview adopts the runtime's week vocabulary is the taker's to measure and say.
- Serial: after PR #20865, which is the writer these readers must match.
- Same family, other surface: #20602 (`/export`, `domain:cli`), which stays its own card.

## Dedupe

`mcp__github__search_issues`, repo-scoped, open and closed, in the act that filed this card:
- 「formatDateBucket year 0050 1970 dimension label unpadded year preview bucketDate below 1000」: 3 hits. #20760 (open) is the core writer and reader, whose PR produced this finding. #20599 (closed) is the instant for 0001..0099. #4033 (closed) is an unrelated bucket-label drop. None covers these two producers.
